SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 54.568056, -130.7075 (Explicit)
Reported Spill Volume: 1215 gallon
Report DescriptionGREEN ISLAND LIGHT STATION REPORTS THE STATION’S DAY TANKS MAY HAVE MALFUNCTIONED, CAUSING AN OVERFILL OF DIESEL OVER NIGHT. THE PRODUCT IS LAND BASED, HOWEVER, AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT HAS ENTERED THE MARINE. LIGHT KEEPER REPORTS SIZEABLE POOLS OF DIESEL ON THE ROCKS, AND THEY ARE CURRENTLY AT LOW TIDE. THEY HAVE DEPLOYED SORBENTS AND ARE ATTEMPTING TO RECOVER SOME OF THE PRODUCT. LIGHT KEEPER ADVISED THEY WILL NOTIFY THE PROVINCE. MEHR DUTY OFFICER NOTIFIED AND ASSESSING. UPDATE 3 - 0449 - 2025 - POL - ROC – DAY TANK FUEL DISCHARGE, GREEN ISLAND LIGHT STATION – UPDATE #2 + AR, 2025-06-03 @ 1732 PDT CCG HELO CONDUCTED AN OVERFLIGHT OF GREEN ISLAND AND THE AFFECTED AREA. A MEHR RESPONSE SPECIALIST OBSERVED THE POLLUTION ACCUMULATING ALONG SEVERAL SECTIONS OF THE NORTH SHORELINE OF GREEN ISLAND. SOUTHERN, SOUTH WESTERN, AND SOUTH EASTERN SHORELINES SHOWING NO PRODUCT (PHOTO ATTACHMENT 1 REFERS). ADDITIONAL SLICKS WERE IDENTIFIED TO THE NORTH OF GREEN ISLAND, EXTENDING APPROXIMATELY 3NM SOUTH OF THE INTERNATIONAL BOUNDARY (PHOTO ATTACHMENT 2 REFERS). THESE REMAINING SLICKS APPEAR TO BE RAPIDLY WEATHERING. GIVEN THE LOCATION AND PREVAILING ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS, THE SLICK AND CONCENTRATIONS ACCUMULATED ALONG THE SHORELINE,IS EXPECTED TO DISSIPATE NATURALLY THROUGH EVAPORATION AND DISPERSION OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL TIDAL CYCLES. CCG MEHR REMAINS ABLE TO ASSIST LEAD AGENCY IF SITUATION CHANGES OR WARRANTS. CCG NAVIGATIONAL PROGRAMS AND DFO REAL PROPERTY AND SAFETY SECURITY IS WORKING AS RESPONSIBLE PARTY AND WILL COORDINATE FOR LAND BASED CLEANUP AND REMEDIATION AS REQUIRED. CCG INDIGENOUS RELATIONSHIPS AND PARTNERSHIPS HAS OPENED LINES OF COMMUNICATION AND WILL CONTINUE TO SHARE UPDATES. ECCC, AS LEAD FEDERAL AGENCY FOR LAND-BASED SPILLS ON FEDERAL PROPERTY AND REGULATOR WILL LEAD INTERAGENCY COORDINATION CALL ON 4 JUNE 2025 AND WILL UTILIZE NORTH COAST INTEGRATED RESPONSE PLAN DISTRIBUTION LIST. ASSESSMENT UNDER CSA PART 8 IS CONCLUDED AT THIS TIME.

Report Description/// 10MAY24 48-HOUR PHMSA UPDATE TO NRC REPORT NUMBER 1398400 /// UPDATED INFORMATION IS AS FOLLOWS: ON WEDNESDAY MAY 08 WILLIAMS CALLED THE NRC TO REPORT AN INCIDENT ON LINE 2443 IN THE NW PIPELINE SYSTEM NEAR THE GLENDALE METER STATION IN GLENDALE, OREGON. THE INCIDENT OCCURRED DURING THE REMOVAL OF COATING ON THE PIPELINE WHILE COMPLETING AN EXPLORATORY DIG BASED ON AN ILI RUN. CAUSE OF THE LEAK IS CURRENTLY UNDER INVESTIGATION AND MORE INFORMATION WILL BE PROVIDED IN THE 30 DAY REPORT, INCLUDING ESTIMATED LEAK VOLUME. THE LEAK WAS TEMPORARILY REMEDIATED WITH A PLIDCO LEAK CLAMP. THERE IS A PRESSURE REDUCTION ON THE LINE SINCE THE ONSET OF THE DIG CONSIDERED REPORTABLE DUE TO AN APPROXIMATE COST TO REPAIR OF $200,000. PERMANENT REPAIR BY CUTOUT IS EXPECTED TO BE COMPLETED 15JUN24. ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION OF INCIDENT: CALLER IS REPORTING THAT WHILE CONDUCTING SOME INVESTIGATIVE DIGGING ON A PIPELINE. THEY DISCOVERED AN ODOR OF NATURAL GAS. THEY USED A LEAK DETECTOR AND FOUND BUBBLES. THIS MAY EXCEED THE DAMAGES COST THRESHOLD OF 139,700 DOLLARS.

THIS AREA IS HISTORICALLY KNOWN AS A NATURAL COLLECTION AREA, USCG INVESTIGATED BOTH UP AND DOWN RIVER AND WERE NOT ABLE TO LOCATE SOURCE, OBSERVED SHEEN NATURALLY ATTENUATE.
